title: Electrode Processes Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A torch glows on a battery and a wall clock ticks for months on one small cell. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Aarav clips a battery lamp onto his bicycle and asks where the electricity really comes from.

You will see zinc dipped in copper sulphate (copper coats the zinc, the blue fades), then the same redox reaction split into the Daniell cell on the molecule bench: zinc gives electrons at the anode, they flow through the wire, copper ions take them at the cathode, the salt bridge closes the circuit and the meter reads 1.1 V. We meet electrode potential and standard electrode potential E° (1 M, 298 K), the standard hydrogen electrode (E° = 0.00 V), the E° ladder (Zn -0.76 V, Cu +0.34 V, gap 1.10 V), the electrochemical series from Li (-3.05 V) to F2 (+2.87 V) and which metal pushes out which. Then a worked zinc-silver cell (1.56 V), the coefficient trap, an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 77 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
